subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives remain non-extracting with delivery-boundary warnings, be extracted as attachments, or stay documented as by-design only?
rationale: The current parser intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported silent skip affects real attachment delivery; changing extraction behavior could turn code examples into media sends.

options.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning where user-visible delivery is normalized, and land the linked PR after the remaining review concern is resolved.

options.title: Extract Fenced Tokens
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the false-positive risk for code examples unless a stricter contract is designed.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning where user-visible delivery is normalized, and land the linked PR after the remaining review concern is resolved.
